text:
mira: Heads up — doing bring-up for redwood-llm-3b-qa q8 on H100 in ap-southeast1. FlashAttn v3 looks faster at p50 but p95 spikes 2.3x compared to Triton vendor kernel for short prompts. Anyone seen similar microburst warmup behavior?

dan: saw this on a different model. usually small-batch tail worsens with continuous batching + flashv3 packing. do you have numbers?
mira: perf-bot posted quick numbers: p50 18ms (flashv3) vs 22ms (triton), p95 160ms (flashv3) vs 75ms (triton). throughput @ 128 tokens: flashv3 420 req/s, triton 390 req/s. link: https://perf.redwood/internal/dash/bringup/1702500000
s-research-bot: auto-bench results attached: run id r-20240210-03. config: q8_k=128, batch_limit=8, sequence=64, tail_window=200ms. flashv3 shows KV-cache priming cost on first few tokens for microbursts.
leo: can you paste the run command + kernel flags? sometimes a missing warmup or packing threshold causes flashv3 to favor a slower codepath.
mira: here —
```
./run_bench --model redwood-llm-3b-qa --quant q8 --kernel flashv3 --batch_limit 8 --pack_threshold 4 --seq 64 --region ap-southeast1
```

dan: try lowering pack_threshold to 1 or increase microburst_warmup to 20ms. flashv3 expects continuous stream to amortize kernel setup. also check CPU-side enqueue jitter.
ops-jen: from infra side we saw higher network jitter in ap-southeast1 during the run window, could amplify p95. I can re-run on a dedicated pool if you want.
mira: can we have a short checklist: when should we prefer Triton vendor kernel vs FlashAttn v3 for production? want a concrete rule for rollout/rollback.
kai: proposal (quick):
- prefer flashv3 by default for batch sizes >= 4 and sustained qps (burst-free)
- prefer triton/vendor for spikey workloads where p95 matters and avg batch <=2
- switch threshold: if p95_flashv3 > p95_triton * 1.6 and throughput gain < 10% => roll back to vendor
- always validate eval quality after quant variant change (nisha-evals)

leo: +1. add a warmup heuristic: within first 30s of a container start, steer microbursts to vendor kernel until observed 95th drops below threshold.
s-research-bot: adding to playbook: kernel_preference: [ {condition: "batch<=2 or bursty", action: "vendor"}, {condition: "sustained_batch>=4", action: "flashv3"}, {condition: "p95_degradation>60%", action: "fallback_vendor"} ]
mira: useful. can we codify this into the runtime selector? something like: `kernel_selector.policy = 'latency-first'` that flips to vendor for tail cases.
dan: yes. runtime flag exists. sample snippet: `kernel_selector.set_policy({mode: 'latency-first', max_batch_for_flash: 3, warmup_ms: 30000})`
ops-jen: re-run on dedicated pool in 15m and tag results here. I'll also attach network traces.
mira: thanks — will re-run with pack_threshold=1 and warmup_ms=30s, plus a vendor-fallback policy enabled. will report back with new perf numbers and eval checks. :thumbsup:
kai: quick note — record the model payload shape distribution (short vs long) in the dashboard. kernel choice should be signal-driven, not manual.
mira: agreed. I'll add a short chart to the dashboard showing batch dist and tail-by-kernel.
leo: if we automate, include a safety cap: don't switch kernels more than once per 10 minutes per host to avoid flapping.
mira: good call. setting hysteresis. thanks all.
s-research-bot: scheduled re-run queued (r-20240210-03b) on dedicated pool. will post results to this thread.
